amendments.title: An offline archive or restore reports success and is silently lost afterwards
amendments.what: Founder, web 2026-09-21: with the network offline, archiving and restoring both work on screen and toast success. Correct as far as verifiedWrite goes — it will not claim a failure it cannot prove — but the consequence is not benign. The optimistic flag is local only, the POST never reached the server, and archivePlan/restorePlan call invalidatePlans(key) regardless, so the next fetch once she is back online pulls the server's pre-archive truth and the card reappears in Your lessons. She archived seven lessons on a school bus with no signal, was told each one moved, and finds them all back with no explanation. 'Say nothing when we cannot prove failure' is right; 'say SUCCESS when we cannot prove success' is the part that misleads.
amendments.fix:
OPEN — founder's to decide, roughly in ascending cost: (a) word the unverified case honestly — on status 'unverified' replace the success toast with something like 'Saved on this device — we couldn't reach Meyy to confirm it', so she is not told a thing happened that may not have; (b) block the act while the app knows it is offline (navigator.onLine / a failed heartbeat) and say so; (c) queue the write and replay it when the connection returns, which is the only option that actually keeps her work and the only one that costs new machinery. Note this is not specific to the archive — every verifiedWrite caller has the same unverified-success shape, so whichever wording is chosen should be decided once and applied across them rather than patched here. Row 05.16's offline expectation and its Android watch note must be rewritten in the same pass.

CLAUDE'S RECOMMENDATION 2026-09-21, asked directly: a fix IS due, but disabling-when-offline is the weaker half and should not be the whole of it. The signal for 'offline' is navigator.onLine, which is false only when the OS reports no interface — it is TRUE on the common Indian school case, a phone or laptop joined to a wifi network whose uplink is dead or captive. So a disable-on-offline guard blocks the narrow airplane-mode case (the one the walk row tests) and lets through the case teachers actually meet, where she would still be told 'Moved to Archive' and still lose it. Order of work: (a) FIRST make the unverified case speak honestly — that covers every way the write can fail to land, however the network is broken, and it is a wording change; (b) THEN add the offline guard if wanted, as a courtesy that saves her the attempt when the OS is certain; (c) queueing and replay only if teachers turn out to work offline in earnest, which rows 05.31/05.32 will tell us. Decide the wording once for all verifiedWrite callers.

★ THE PATTERN TO COPY ALREADY EXISTS IN THE PRODUCT (found at 05.30, 2026-09-22). The Year Plan Word export handles exactly this case well: offline it prints, under the totals row, 'Couldn't download the year plan. Couldn't reach Meyy just now. Tap the arrow to try again.' — an in-window line rather than an alert, naming the failure, naming the control to retry, and distinguishing an unreachable server from a 404 or a 501. That is the shape the report download (05.18) and the archive (this amendment) both owe. Do not invent new wording: take this one as the template, since a teacher should meet one voice for 'the network did not answer' wherever she meets it.

[FIXED web 2026-09-24T01:40:44] Option (a), the honest wording, as recommended. MyLessonPlans.jsx verifyArchive now handles status 'unverified' explicitly, BEFORE the mismatch branch: nothing is reverted (the verdict 'we do not know that it failed' stands), but the cheerful toast is replaced with 'Archived on this device — we couldn't reach Meyy to confirm it.' / 'Restored on this device — we couldn't reach Meyy to confirm it.' Wording follows the Year Plan export's offline line, the one place in the product that already does this well.
NOT DONE, and deliberately: (b) blocking the act when navigator.onLine is false, and (c) queue and replay. (b) would block airplane mode and let through the case teachers actually meet — a wifi with a dead uplink, where onLine is true; (c) is real machinery and should wait for evidence from rows 05.31/05.32 that teachers work offline in earnest.
⚠️ OTHER verifiedWrite CALLERS STILL SAY SUCCESS ON 'unverified' — this fixes the archive pair only. The sentence above is now the template; apply it to the rest (the readiness save, the prepared-plan mark, section state) in one pass rather than inventing wording each time.

That is the better sentence and the right destination, but it is a PROMISE OF A REPLAY the app does not keep — there is no queue, and invalidatePlans means the next successful fetch pulls the server's pre-archive truth back over her change, so the lesson reappears unexplained. Two routes: (A) build the queue-and-replay — unconfirmed writes held in device storage, retried when a request next succeeds or the app foregrounds, the listing refreshed only after; one sitting of real work in the shared layer, serving both surfaces and every other write that can fail offline, and it also answers 05.32's offline story. amendments.title: Report filenames should carry the chapter NAME, not the chapter number
amendments.what: Founder, 2026-09-22, on seeing the downloads: 'with the splits we did in English especially, chapter number is an issue'. Today api/main.py builds one base for all three reports — base = f'grade-{grade}-{_safe_name(subject)}-ch{cn}' — giving lesson-plan-grade-iii-english-ch13 / assessment-grade-iii-english-ch13-answers / integrated-grade-iii-english-ch13-answers (api/main.py:3565, 3573, 3584). Since English chapters are SPLIT into their constituent sections, the chapter number no longer identifies what the teacher is holding, and it is not what she searches by — she searches by chapter name. She may also rename the file, which a number-based name invites.
amendments.fix:
FOUNDER'S PROPOSAL, to be implemented at the fix point:
  LP-{class}-{Subject}-{chapter name}
  Assess-{class}-{Subject}-{chapter name}
  Assess-Answers-{class}-{Subject}-{chapter name}
  LP-Assess-{class}-{Subject}-{chapter name}
  LP-Assess-Answers-{class}-{Subject}-{chapter name}
e.g. LP-III-English-{chapter name}. Rationale: lets her retrieve by searching the chapter and index her files easily.
FOUR THINGS THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST SETTLE, all found while locating the code:
(1) PUNCTUATION. Chapter titles carry apostrophes, exclamation marks and brackets — live examples from this very account: "Thank God! (Thank God!)", "Madhu's Wish (Madhu's Wish)", "Out in the Garden (Toys and Games)". _safe_name (or a new slug rule) must handle these, and the result must stay valid on Windows, macOS and Android (Windows forbids \ / : * ? " < > |).
(2) THE DOUBLED PARENTHETICAL. Post-split English titles read '{section} ({chapter})' and collapse to 'Thank God! (Thank God!)' when the two are the same. That reads badly in a filename and is worth de-duplicating at the same time.
(3) LENGTH. A long title plus prefix can exceed what mail clients and Windows paths handle comfortably — cap it (say 60-80 chars) and truncate the NAME, never the prefix.
(4) THE UNIT VARIANT. The integrated report already appends '-unit{n}' when scoped to one unit (api/main.py:3583); the proposed scheme does not say where that goes. Decide its slot.
One base string feeds all three call sites, so this is a single change in api/main.py — but the five names differ by KIND and by the answers flag, which the present code expresses as suffixes; the proposal puts them in the prefix, so the naming needs to move into a small helper rather than stay as an f-string plus suffix.

FIVE POINTS OF FEEDBACK ON THE SCHEME (Claude, asked 2026-09-22; founder has already accepted that exclamation marks are dropped when naming):
(1) WHERE 'Answers' SITS — a real trade-off, founder's call. Early (his scheme) makes the one file she must not hand to students unmissable, and it survives truncation in narrow file lists, which cut the END of a name. Late (Assess-III-English-{name}-Answers) keeps each pair together in a sorted folder — under the prefix form, ALL the answers files cluster away from their plain twins, so the two versions of one chapter sit far apart. Safety argues early, retrieval argues late.
(2) ROMAN vs ARABIC CLASS. 'III' does not sort: a folder spanning classes orders I, II, III, IV, IX, V, VI — alphabetically, which is wrong numerically. Zero-padded Arabic ('03') sorts correctly and reads fine. The app itself shows 'Class 3' in My Lessons and Roman elsewhere, so either is defensible — but pick one deliberately.
(3) THE PUNCTUATION AND SEPARATOR RULE, written down once. Drop ! and ? (accepted); drop apostrophes rather than substituting (Madhu's → Madhus); strip the Windows-illegal set \ / : * ? " < > | ; collapse the de-duplicated brackets; and choose hyphens or spaces and hold to it. Spaces are legal everywhere and read better, but become %20 in a mail link and are awkward on a command line — hyphens are the safer default given teachers mail these files.
(4) NOTHING DISTINGUISHES TWO DOWNLOADS OF THE SAME CHAPTER. Prepare again, re-download, and the browser appends '(1)' — so her folder holds 'LP-III-English-Madhus Wish' and 'LP-III-English-Madhus Wish (1)' with nothing to say which is the current plan. plan_date is already passed to every builder and is on the page; consider whether it belongs in the name too. Against: it lengthens every filename for a case that is not the common one.
(5) KIND FIRST vs CHAPTER FIRST. Kind-first (his scheme) groups a folder by document type across all chapters; chapter-first would group the five files belonging to one chapter. Since the stated rationale is SEARCH by chapter name, kind-first costs nothing — noted only so the sort behaviour is a choice rather than a surprise.

It is built on its own path (POST /api/year-plan/export-docx), so it will not pick the new scheme up by accident. Decide its name in the same pass so every file Meyy hands a teacher looks like one family, e.g. YearPlan-III-English.

amendments.title: Preparing a chapter again does not replace anything — the copy must say so (founder chose to keep the behaviour)
amendments.what:
Founder, web 2026-09-22: regenerate an already-prepared chapter and (1) with DIFFERENT periods two plans end up sitting for the same chapter; (2) with the SAME periods only one remains, and it is the previously existing plan — an attached lesson is unaffected.
MECHANISM, confirmed: a served plan's filename carries the PERIOD MATRIX. api/data.genon_plan_filename() builds ch_{NN}_{norm_matrix(matrix)}_e{engine}_c{canonical_version}.json (e.g. ch_05_50m16_e07_c20260726112240.json). Same periods → identical filename → the serve cache returns the existing file untouched, which is exactly why the old plan survives and the binding is unaffected. Different periods → a different filename → a second plan file, a second key in her prepared register, a second card on the shelf.
★ THE SHARP EDGE IS THE PROMISE. The CTA hint and the confirm window both say preparing again 'replaces the tracked version'. In the same-periods case nothing is replaced because nothing changed; in the different-periods case nothing is replaced either — a sibling is ADDED, and the section binding still points at the OLD file, so the tracked version is precisely the one thing left untouched. The row's 'no duplicate card is added' fails with it.
Two plans per chapter is not itself absurd — a 16-period and a 19-period ch 5 are genuinely different artefacts and the architecture keys them apart on purpose. What is wrong is that the product PROMISES replacement, delivers accumulation, and leaves two cards on the shelf distinguishable only by their duration line.

★ THE OWED CHECK IS DONE, 2026-09-22, and the answer is the worse one: with the chapter attached and prepared again at a different period count, the SECTION CARD KEEPS THE ORIGINAL duration's plan — the binding does not follow. So the hint does not merely overstate; it states the opposite of what happens. Separately, a NEW section is then offered BOTH durations to choose from in the attach picker.
amendments.fix:
OPEN — founder decides which promise is the true one, and the wording follows:
(A) REPLACEMENT IS THE PROMISE (what the copy says today): on confirming, re-point the section binding to the new file and retire the superseded plan — archive it, or delete her prepared mark for it — so one chapter leaves one card. Needs a decision about a plan she may have exported or taught from.
(B) ACCUMULATION IS THE TRUTH (what the code does): reword the hint and the confirm window to say so — 'preparing again at a different length creates a second plan for this chapter; your class keeps the one it is teaching' — and make the two cards tell themselves apart on the shelf beyond a duration line. The row's 'no duplicate card' clause would then need rewriting too.
Either way, ONE CHECK IS OWED FIRST and it decides how bad this is: attach a chapter to a section, prepare it again with a DIFFERENT period count, and see whether the section card follows the new plan or stays on the old one. If it stays — which the filename mechanism says it must — then the hint is not merely loose, it is the opposite of what happens.

★ WHAT THE CHECK IMPLIES FOR THE CHOICE. It weakens (A) and strengthens (B). The two plans turn out to be USEFUL rather than clutter: a new section is offered both lengths and can take the one that suits its timetable, which is a real benefit and is what the period-keyed filename was designed to allow. Retiring the superseded plan under (A) would destroy that, and would also break a plan she may already be teaching from in another section. So the recommended shape is (B): keep the accumulation, tell the truth about it, and make the shelf and the picker distinguish two lengths of one chapter properly rather than by a duration line alone. The copy then has two jobs — say that a different length creates a second plan, and say that the class she is teaching keeps the plan it is on. Founder's call.

★ FOUNDER'S DECISION, 2026-09-22: option (B). The behaviour STAYS — a different length keeps making a second plan, because a new section can then take whichever length suits it — and the WORDING is fixed to say that the existing plan is not overwritten. Nothing is retired, nothing is re-pointed; this is a copy change plus a row-text change.
TWO PLACES CARRY THE COPY (web PrepareLesson.jsx ~644-660, and the same strings on the phone): the hint under the CTA, and the confirm window's body. amendments.what:
Founder, web 2026-09-22: with every request carrying a token the server rejects, the app does not end the session or return to sign-in — it carries on normally. ★ CAUSE. Whether a 401 signs her out depends entirely on WHICH call happens to fail, and the most common one swallows it. packages/shared/src/plans.js fetchPlans throws on any non-ok status and then catches with: 'Offline, CORS, a 5xx — the stored copy stands, unmarked, so the next mount tries again … if (stored && stored.plans) return stored.plans'. A 401 is none of those things, but it takes the same branch, so a teacher with a cached listing — which is every returning teacher — sees her lessons as usual and the refusal is invisible. Rolling the subject wheel is exactly this path, which is why the test looked like nothing happened.
★ AND THE RULE IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THIS CODEBASE, one module away. packages/shared/src/account.js states it in its own comment: '⚠️ A 401 is the server REFUSING this session, not a network failure — never fall back to a cached identity for a refused one. Everything else keeps what we hold', and implements it as `if (String(e.message) === "401") throw e;`. page.jsx:529 then signs her out on that throw. So the contract exists and is correct; plans.js simply does not honour it, and the other cached fetchers need checking for the same omission.
CONSEQUENCE: a teacher whose session has expired goes on using a half-working app — reads come from her device copy, every write silently fails — until she happens to touch the one path that propagates the refusal. That is worse than being signed out, because nothing tells her why her work is not saving.
amendments.fix:
OPEN. (a) Adopt account.js's rule in plans.js: rethrow on 401 rather than falling back to the stored copy, so the refusal reaches page.jsx's handler. (b) AUDIT EVERY OTHER CACHED FETCHER for the same swallow — readiness, section-state, section-history, entitlement, the Ask Meyy bank — the rule should be stated once and applied everywhere, not repeated by hand in six catches. The cleanest shape is a single helper that classifies a failure as 'refused' versus 'unreachable', which is the same distinction WALK-A-064, WALK-A-071 and 05.18's offline download all need for their own reasons; consider doing all of it in one piece of work. (c) On the phone the same audit applies, and the row's divergence note says the phone handles 401 on the screen while the web handles it at page level — check both end up signing out.
TEST NOTE for the re-walk, so the next person does not lose an hour: mangling the stored token does NOT work (supabase-js keeps the live session in memory). Patch window.fetch to rewrite the Authorization header instead, and make sure throttling is OFF — an offline browser makes every outcome look like success from cache.

WHY NOT IN plans.js: that rethrow was written first and REVERTED. There are 22 raw fetches in the web components and 5 more in the shared package, and each caller swallows its own error (`.catch(() => setPlans([]))`), so a rethrow would only have produced an empty shelf and the rule would have had to be repeated 27 times — the drift this codebase has already paid for three times (14-vs-19, ppw_from_annual across two languages, and WALK-A-074's own split). Consequently the 'audit every other cached fetcher' item is now MOOT for the session-refusal purpose: any 401 from the API signs her out regardless of which call met it.
Two deliberate narrowings: only responses from our own API base count, so a 401 from Supabase's token endpoint (which supabase-js handles by refreshing) can never sign her out; and a refusal arriving before the shell has registered its handler is remembered and replayed on registration, so a 401 during the first paint is not lost.

amendments.title: Marking a unit complete offline looks saved, then silently vanishes — and the save check cannot see the pointer at all
amendments.what:
Founder, web 2026-09-24: offline, he marked the first unit of English IV ch 12 complete. The class card showed it. He went back online, returned — and the completion was gone. No warning at any point. His question: 'should it not have warned the first time it is offline?' Yes.
★ SAME MECHANISM AS WALK-A-064, ON THE MOST IMPORTANT WRITE IN THE PRODUCT. setUnitPointer writes the pointer to the device, then pushSectionState → syncSectionNow → verifiedWrite. Offline the write fails (swallowed by design) and the verifying read fails too, so the status is 'unverified' — and syncSectionNow acts ONLY on 'mismatch', so nothing is said. When the connection returns, the section-state reconcile (pullSectionState, the 20s sync) pulls the server's older pointer over the device copy and the completion disappears. The archive losing a lesson from a shelf is an annoyance; a teacher who marks her way through a lesson in a classroom with no signal and finds her progress reset has lost the one record the tracker exists to keep.
★ SECOND, INDEPENDENT FINDING — THE CHECK IS BLIND TO THE POINTER. syncSectionNow builds its expectation as `want = { chapter, done }` and packages/shared/src/verify.js sectionStateMatches compares chapter and done ONLY. The unit pointer — the very thing 'Mark this unit complete' changes — is not part of the read-after-write check. So even ONLINE, a pointer write that landed wrong, or not at all, would read back as 'ok' provided the chapter binding was intact. The check reports on the fact that did not change and is silent about the one that did.
amendments.fix:
OPEN — and it decides WALK-A-064's open question for both.
(1) THE POINTER JOINS THE CHECK, regardless of anything else: `want` gains `unit`, and sectionStateMatches compares it (normalising the 'absent means 0' convention setUnitPointer uses, or the check will report a mismatch for unit 0). Small, certain, and it makes every later fix verifiable. Also worth including the bookmark if it is meant to be durable.
(2) THEN THE REAL QUESTION, which the founder was already weighing at 064: honest wording (B) or queue-and-replay (A). For the archive, B was tolerable — she can archive again. For MARK-COMPLETE it is not: 'not saved to Meyy — check your connection' asks a teacher mid-lesson to remember and redo her progress later, and the classroom is exactly where the signal is worst. This is the case that justifies A. Two concrete callers now need the same machinery — the archive pair and section state — and both already funnel through verifiedWrite, so a queue there serves both: hold unverified writes on the device; retry them when a request next succeeds or the app foregrounds; and do NOT let the reconcile pull the server's older state over a section with a write still queued (that last clause is what actually stops the vanishing — without it, a replay would race the pull and lose).
(3) IF A WAITS, B AS A STOPGAP, using 064's sentence as the template: 'Marked complete here, but not saved to Meyy — check your connection.' Better than silence, but it is a warning, not a fix.
Founder's call on (2)/(3). (1) should be done either way.
[FIXED shared 2026-09-24 — founder chose (2), queue-and-replay] Lives in packages/shared, so web AND phone get it at once.
(1) The pointer joined the check: sectionStateMatches compares want.unit to row.unit_index, with absent/null/'' all meaning unit 0.
(2) A persisted, owner-stamped PENDING MARK per section (lu_pending_{sk} = {owner, ts}). Every local write sets it; a push the server confirms clears it (only if no newer write arrived meanwhile — the ts guard). An 'unverified' push keeps it.
(3) The reconcile (pullSectionState, the existing 20s/focus timer) does NOT adopt the server's row for a section with a pending mark of hers — it re-sends ours instead. That is the retry, and the clause that actually stops the vanishing.
(4) Found while testing: if the signal returned WHILE the check's read was retrying, that read succeeded and disagreed, was taken as 'mismatch', and the server's older pointer was adopted — the same loss by another door. A request that got no response at all is now never a mismatch; an HTTP refusal still is (else a write the server will never take would freeze the section against other devices).
(5) Cross-account guards: a mark left by another teacher on this browser is discarded unsent; a push waiting behind an offline retry does not run if the signed-in teacher has changed; sign-out sweeps lu_pending_.
Tests: packages/shared/test/sectionPending.test.js, 8 tests; the two new guards were mutation-checked (removing each makes its test fail). Shared suite 231/231.
NOT in this fix: an on-screen word while offline. With the queue, the honest line becomes 'saved here, will reach Meyy when you're back online' — founder's wording call, and it belongs with 064's archive, which could adopt the same queue.
